subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced final-reply `MEDIA:` tokens stay non-delivered with a delivery-boundary warning, or should OpenClaw extract standalone valid `MEDIA:` tokens from code fences?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported user problem is silent media loss; changing extraction behavior could mutate legitimate code examples, while warn-only leaves delivery behavior unchanged.

options.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
options.body: Review and land the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80396 shape so fenced tokens remain visible text but emit one delivery-boundary warning when skipped.

options.title: Extract fenced standalone tokens
options.body: Change the parser contract to deliver valid standalone fenced `MEDIA:` tokens, accepting the risk that examples can become attachments.

options.title: Document as by design
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96275, leaving the runtime skip silent unless another diagnostic path is added.

recommendation.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
recommendation.body: Review and land the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80396 shape so fenced tokens remain visible text but emit one delivery-boundary warning when skipped.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the most recent owner of the exact parser/test lines on main and are well positioned to decide whether the warning-only contract fits the current runtime boundary.
